capture.final_message:
The two equivalences connect unrelated statements, so the clean strategy is to prove all four component assertions independently and assemble each `Iff` using constant implications.

- For the first assertion, view the pointwise action `s • N` as the submodule generated by all `a • N` with `a ∈ s`. Its universal property is exactly the lattice supremum `⨆ a ∈ s, a • N`.
- For the map identity, characterize `I • N` by finite sums of terms `r • n` with `r ∈ I`. Linearity gives `f (r • n) = r • f n`, yielding both inclusions between `map f (I • N)` and `I • map f N`.
- For the evaluation assertion, use finite-field multivariable interpolation. Every function on the finite set `σ → K` is a linear combination of point-indicator polynomials, obtained as products of univariate Lagrange polynomials. Each variable has degree at most `|K| - 1`, so these polynomials lie in `MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fintype.card K - 1)`, proving that its image under `evalₗ` is `⊤`. Finiteness of both `K` and `σ` is essential here.
- The final assertion follows from closure of a subfield under finite sums, applied by `Finset.sum_mem`.

After establishing these four lemmas, each direction of either `Iff` simply discards its hypothesis and invokes the independently proved target.
